extracted.intended_audience: members of PRISA; public relations practitioners and communication/communication management professionals in Southern Africa (consultancies, in-house, consultants' chapter)
extracted.subtask_description: A regional code of ethics and professional standards for public relations and communication management, intended to set conduct, disclosure, competence, and enforcement expectations for PRISA members and affiliated practitioners in Southern Africa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional attributes (preamble)
rubrics_metrics.description: A profession is distinguished by certain characteristics or attributes, including: Mastery of a particular intellectual skill through education and training; Acceptance of duties to a broader society than merely one’s clients/employers; Objectivity; High standards of conduct and performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These attributes set the normative baseline for members' behaviour and signal duties beyond narrow commercial aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: We base our professional principles on the fundamental value and dignity of the individual. We believe in and support the free exercise of human rights, especially freedom of speech, freedom of assembly and freedom of the media... In serving the interests of clients and employers, we dedicate ourselves to the goals of better communication, mutual understanding and co-operation among diverse individuals, groups and institutions of society. We also subscribe to and support equal opportunity of employment in the public relations and communication profession and lifelong professional development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principles express commitments to human rights, public-interest communication, diversity, equal opportunity and continuing professional development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pledge: conduct with truth, accuracy, fairness and responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: to conduct ourselves professionally, with truth, accuracy, fairness and responsibility to the public and towards our colleagues and to an informed society;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members explicitly pledge truthfulness and responsibility in communications and relations with colleagues and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pledge: improve competence and advance knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: to improve our individual competence and advance the knowledge and proficiency of the profession through continuing education and research;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members commit to ongoing professional development and contributing to the profession's knowledge base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pledge: adhere to PRISA Code and Global Protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: to adhere to the articles of the Code of Ethics and Professional Standards for the Practice of Public Relations and Communication Management in Southern Africa and to adhere to the principles of the Global protocol on Ethics in Public Relations and Communication Management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members must subscribe to both the local PRISA Code and international/global ethics protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of public relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Public relations is the management, through communication, of perceptions and strategic relationships between an organisation and its internal and external stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This functional definition frames the scope and objectives of acceptable professional practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Conduct: protect and enhance the profession (2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall acknowledge that there is an obligation to protect and enhance the profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members must act to safeguard the reputation and standing of the public relations profession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Conduct: keep informed and educated (2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall keep informed and educated about practices in the profession that ensures ethical conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing awareness of best practice and ethical developments is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Conduct: pursue personal professional development (2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall actively pursue personal professional development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members are expected to take initiative in their own learning and skills improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Conduct: commitment to ethical practices and public trust (2.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: We are committed to ethical practices, preservation of public trust, and the pursuit of communication excellence with powerful standards of performance, professionalism, and ethical conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical practice and public trust are central organizational values guiding behaviour and standards of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Conduct: accurately define PR activity limits (2.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall accurately define what public relations activities can and cannot accomplish. In the conduct of our professional activities, we shall respect the public interest and the dignity of the individual. It is our responsibility at all times to deal fairly and honestly with our clients or employers, past or present, with our colleagues, media communication and with the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overpromising; uphold fairness and honesty toward clients, colleagues and the public; respect individual dignity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Conduct: act in accordance with public interest (2.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall conduct our professional lives in accordance with the public interest. We shall not conduct ourselves in any manner detrimental to the profession of public relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional actions must consider public interest and avoid harm to the profession's reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Conduct: maintain integrity, accuracy and good taste (2.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: We have a positive duty to maintain integrity and accuracy, as well as generally accepted standards of good taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards include not only factual accuracy but also professional decorum and 'good taste' norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Conduct: avoid false or misleading information (2.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall not knowingly, intentionally or recklessly communicate false or misleading information. It is our obligation to use proper care to avoid doing so inadvertently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits deliberate or reckless misinformation and requires due care to prevent accidental misinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Conduct: do not guarantee specified results or contingency-only payment (2.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall not guarantee the achievement of specified results beyond our direct control. We shall not negotiate nor agree terms with a prospective employer or client on the basis of payment only contingent upon specific future public relations achievements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoiding misleading promises and unethical contingency payment arrangements tied to outcomes outside PR control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Conduct: respect other professions' codes (2.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall, when acting for a client or employer, who belongs to a profession, respect the code of ethics of that other profession and shall not knowingly be party to any breach of such a code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When working across professions, members must honour the ethical rules of the other profession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Conduct: obey laws and correct violations (2.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall obey laws and public policies governing our professional activities and will be sensitive to the spirit of all laws and regulations and, should any law or public policy be violated, for whatever reason, act promptly to correct the situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with legal and public policy obligations and proactive correction of violations are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Conduct: credit sources and identify information purposes (2.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall give credit for unique expressions borrowed from others and identify the sources and purposes of all information disseminated to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper attribution and transparency about information sources and intent are mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct towards Clients/Employers: safeguard confidences (3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall safeguard the confidences of both present and former clients and employers. We shall not disclose or make use of information given or obtained in confidence from an employer or client, past or present, for personal gain or otherwise, or to the disadvantage or prejudice of such client or employer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidentiality of client and employer information is a core obligation; no misuse for personal gain or prejudice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct towards Clients/Employers: avoid conflicts without consent (3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall not represent conflicting or competing interests without the express consent of those involved, given after full disclosure of the facts. We shall not place ourselves in a position where our interests are or may be in conflict with a duty to a client, without full disclosure of such interests to all involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full disclosure and consent are required before accepting potentially conflicting or competing representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct towards Clients/Employers: no disguised or undisclosed interests; disclose payments (3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall not be party to any activity which seeks to dissemble or mislead by promoting one disguised or undisclosed interest whilst appearing to further another. It is our duty to ensure that the actual interest of any organisation with which we may be professionally concerned is adequately declared. In the course of our professional services to the employer or client we shall not accept payment either in cash or in kind in connection with these services from another source without the express consent of our employer or client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires transparency about actual client interests and disclosure/consent for third-party payments or benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct towards Colleagues: do not maliciously injure (4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall not maliciously injure the professional reputation or practice of another individual engaged in the public relations profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits unfounded attacks or malicious actions against colleagues' reputations or practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct towards Colleagues: uphold and cooperate in enforcing the Code (4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall at all times uphold this Code, co-operate with colleagues in doing so and in enforcing decisions on any matter arising from this application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collective responsibility to uphold and assist enforcement of the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct towards Colleagues: registered individuals causing breaches deemed culpable (4.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered individuals who knowingly cause or permit another person or organisation to act in a manner inconsistent with this Code or are party to such an action shall be deemed to be in breach of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accountability extends to those who permit or enable breaches by others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct towards Colleagues: duty to report suspected breaches (4.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If we have reason to believe that another colleague has engaged in practices which may be in breach of this Code, or practices which may be unethical, unfair or illegal, it is our duty to advise the Institute promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligation to report suspected unethical, unfair, or illegal practitioner conduct to PRISA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct towards Colleagues: do not solicit client employees (4.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall not invite any employee of a client to consider alternative employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits poaching client personnel while engaged on their behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct towards the Business Environment: avoid undisclosed financial interest recommendations (5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall not recommend the use of any organisation in which we have a financial interest, nor make use of its services on behalf of our clients or employers, without declaring our interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full disclosure is required when there is a financial interest in recommended organisations or service providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct towards the Business Environment: fees and commissions disclosure (5.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: In performing professional services for a client or employer we shall not accept fees, commissions or any other consideration from anyone other than the client or employer in connection with those services, without the express consent of the client/employer, given after disclosure of the facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving third-party payments requires prior disclosure and express client/employer consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct towards the Business Environment: sever relations if contrary to Code (5.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall sever relations, as soon as possible, with any organisation or individual if such a relationship requires conduct contrary to this Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligation to terminate relationships that would force Code violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct towards the Channels of Communication: do not corrupt integrity of channels (6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall not engage in any practice which tends to corrupt the integrity of channels or media of communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect the impartiality and integrity of media and communication channels; avoid practices that undermine them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct towards the Channels of Communication: identify client/employer publicly (6.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall identify publicly the name of the client or employer on whose behalf any public communication is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency requirement: communications must disclose the sponsoring client or employer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct towards the State: respect constitutional principles (7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: We respect the principles contained in the Constitution of the country in which we are resident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members must respect and operate consistent with the constitutional principles of their jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct towards the State: do not bribe public officials (7.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall not offer or give any reward to any person holding public office, with intent to further our interests or those of our employer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit prohibition on bribery or improper rewards to public officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct towards PRISA: respect PRISA dignity and authority (8.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall at all times respect the dignity and authority of PRISA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members owe deference to the institute's authority and its role in maintaining standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct towards PRISA: uphold registration fees (8.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: We are bound to uphold the annual registration fee levied by PRISA, which fee is payable as determined by the PRISA Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative obligation to pay membership/registration fees as set by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication obligations: encourage widest communication of the Code (9.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: PRISA encourages the widest possible communication about its Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institute promotes dissemination and awareness of the Code among members and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication obligations: Code availability and reuse with credit (9.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRISA Code of Ethics and Professional Standards for the Practice of Public Relations and Communication Management is freely available to all. Permission is hereby granted to any individual or organisation wishing to copy and incorporate all or part of the PRISA Code into personal and corporate codes, with the understanding that appropriate credit be given to PRISA in any publication of such codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Code is freely reusable with required attribution to PRISA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication obligations: institute publications on ethics (9.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Institute’s magazine, Communika publishes periodic articles dealing with ethical issues. At least one session at the annual conference is devoted to ethics. The national office of PRISA through its professional development activities encourages and supports efforts by PRISA student chapter, professional chapters and region to conduct meetings and workshops devoted to the topic of ethics and the PRISA Code. New and renewing members of PRISA sign the following statement as part of their application: 'I have read, understand and subscribe to the PRISA Code of Ethics and Professional Standards for Public Relations and Communication Management.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRISA supports ethics education and requires members to acknowledge understanding and subscription to the Code upon registration/renewal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement and sanctions (10)
rubrics_metrics.description: PRISA fosters compliance with its Code by engaging in global communication campaigns rather than through negative sanctions. However, in keeping with the 2.11 article of the PRISA Code, members of PRISA who are found guilty by the PRISA Disciplinary committee or an appropriate governmental or judicial body of violating laws and public policies governing their professional activities may have their membership terminated by the PRISA board following procedures set forth in the Institute’s bylaws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on positive compliance and education, but explicit retention of disciplinary processes including potential termination of membership for serious violations (disciplinary committee or judicial/govt findings). The Board may bar or expel members convicted or sanctioned for actions violating the Code.
